items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had seen him a few months ago and he was in good health at that time

ctx.x: For the tour, the rhythm section was the same as the last tour, Bishop, De Haas and Starling. I also engaged a girl singer from Trinidad named Cecily Forde who had not been in France very long. We rehearsed for about a week, I finished at the Metro Jazz the 30th of September and we left for Aachen, Germany, the first of October and played our first concert the 2nd in Aachen. We played 70 towns from the 2nd of October until the 15th of December with only six days off.

We were in Kassel the 10th of November when someone in the orchestra had bought a U.S. army paper called Stars and Stripes in which there was an announcement that "Hot Lips Page" had died. I had seen him a few months ago and he was in good health at that time and we had not heard anything about him being sick. To my estimation the world had lost the greatest blues trumpeter who could sing them as well as play them. He also had given Lily and I an autographed recording of his, recorded on Columbia. The titles were…

There were a very few towns that we did not play in West Germany, large and small. We played some concerts for the German public and many concerts were for British military camps. The camps concerts were usually done in the non commissioned officers' (N.C.O.) recreation halls and those fellows really showed us a swell time in every camp we played. They enjoyed jazz and enjoyed showing us how much they appreciated what we had to offer. After the concerts we were offered drinks no end, food for each musician and…

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The American musicians presented at this festival were ... Oran "Hot Lips" Page ... and myself.

ctx.x: The big thing in jazz from the 8th of May until the 15th was the jazz festival that Charles Delaunay organized in collaboration with Frank Bauer, Eddie Barclay and Jacques Souplet. Sidney Bechet and Charlie(the Bird) Parker were the stars, but there were other musicians that were already in the limelight, whose names were to become much better known than they were in 1949. The American musicians presented at this festival were Bechet, Parker, "Big Chief" Russell Moore, Oran "Hot Lips" Page, Kenny Dorham, Tommie…

Jazz was jumping in Paris that week at the Salle Pleyel and jazz fans from different countries (mostly those who had musicians that were favoured in the places they were from) were here to take in the festival and all the jazz clubs were jumping and especially the club St. Germain des Pres on the left bank of Paris, because the American musicians and some from other countries would go jamming after the nightly concerts or on nights when they did not have to appear with Rostaing(clarinet) Braslavsky(clarinet)…

One day during the festival, I went to see "Big Chief" Moore at his hotel. Russell is a real indian and the only one I ever knew that played jazz. I didn't know his weight exactly, but roughly guessing, it must have been at the time about 350 pounds. I tqas about 12:30 a.m. when I knocked on his door and he was still in bed. When he asked who was there. I told him and he said:'Just a minute'. I was waiting almost 10 minutes before he finally opened the door.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We loved him very much and it was shocking and painful when we heard that he died of an attack 6 months later.

ctx.x: Charlie Shavers was leading the other group at the Metropole and the joint was jumping every night. Red featured a song called "Kiss the Baby" and any fellow that was with a woman, Red would ask if she was the baby. If the fellow said yes, then Red would tell him to kiss the baby and he would insist until the fellow kissed the woman. He had me kissing Lily in public at least twice every time we went to the place. Another thing he would do was when a musician came into the bar, that he knew, and he knew many, Red…

"Lips" Page who had a son of 15 years old, was remarried with a school teacher, Elysabeth. They invited us for dinner and we enjoyed being with them. Lips was a natural born joker and terrific company. We stayed late and told him that we wanted to get back to our hotel and wanted to look for a cab. He said that it was not necessary. He would take us back as he had a big new model Cadillac but had to go in the street to look for someone who could drive it. We didn't dig it. Why couldn't he drive it himself? He…

Lily did not like the city of New York very much. She thought that the hotels and also the streets were dirty, that people were upset with money and talked about it all the time, that Americans were very rude. She couldn't stand racism and so was partial with white Americans. But she loved my friends and the jazz scene.
